problem_class.label: nonconvex
problem_class.details: Each component fᵢ has an Lᵢ-Lipschitz gradient, with Lᵢ ≥ 0. Components and their average may be nonconvex. The average F is bounded below by some a with F(x₀) − a ≤ Δ.

problem_class.label: finite_sum
problem_class.details: F(x) = (1/n)∑ᵢ fᵢ(x), with n ≥ 1 and one component per worker. The average (1/n)∑ᵢ Lᵢ bounds the smoothness of F.

oracle.label: stochastic_gradient
oracle.details: At every x, the jointly measurable oracle gᵢ satisfies E[gᵢ(x,ξ)] = ∇fᵢ(x). Each worker consumes consecutive fresh samples from its own IID stream with law μᵢ. The streams are independent across workers.

oracle.label: component_gradient
oracle.details: Worker i can query its own component fᵢ at a point x. A query specifies a positive batch size m and returns a list of m local gradient samples at x.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/DistributedComponentSmoothNonconvex.lean, spec.ComputeQuery and spec.admissible. LongTails/Setups/BandwidthHeterogeneousSmoothNonconvex.lean, ComputeQuery, ComputeReply and computation

distinctive_assumptions.label: bounded_variance
distinctive_assumptions.details: Each worker has its own public bound σᵢ ≥ 0. At every x, E‖gᵢ(x,ξ) − ∇fᵢ(x)‖² ≤ σᵢ². The bound concerns noise around the local component gradient.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: The query and output space is Euclidean ℝᵈ, with public dimension d.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/DistributedComponentSmoothNonconvex.lean, Params.d, Point and spec.Output. LongTails/Setups/BandwidthHeterogeneousSmoothNonconvex.lean, Point. LongTails/Setups/DistributedSmoothNonconvex.lean, Point

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: A batch of m samples occupies worker i for m hᵢ time, with hᵢ > 0 and one pending batch per worker. Workers can compute concurrently with one another and with communication. Each ordered pair has its own FIFO link. Sending k payload bits takes l + b(k + 64) time once the link is available, with l,b ≥ 0. All setup parameters, including x₀, Δ, ε and the worker-specific hᵢ, Lᵢ, σᵢ, are public. The component functions, oracle maps and sampling laws are hidden.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/DistributedComponentSmoothNonconvex.lean, Params, spec.publicInput, spec.valid and spec.admissible. LongTails/Setups/BandwidthHeterogeneousSmoothNonconvex.lean, computation and communication. LongTails/TemplateDistributed.lean, Time, clockBits and step

accuracy.label: gradient_norm_squared
accuracy.details: The designated root returns a measurable point X by the stated elapsed-time deadline. The criterion uses the squared Euclidean norm of the gradient of the full average F at X.

accuracy.label: expected
accuracy.details: ‖∇F(X)‖² must be integrable and E‖∇F(X)‖² ≤ ε² for ε > 0. The expectation uses the product law of the algorithm seed and the oracle streams. The elapsed-time budget is fixed.
accuracy.evidence: LongTails/Setups/DistributedComponentSmoothNonconvex.lean, spec.valid and spec.successful. LongTails/TemplateDistributed.lean, law and TimedConvergence

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: The stationarity problem couples worker-specific smoothness and noise bounds with unequal sampling times and concurrent, bit-priced communication. Success is measured at a root worker under a fixed elapsed-time deadline.
